## WEEK'S BEST IDEA

The seam pattern from doc 2418: route every external read through a named failover layer that logs the switch. It's infrastructure that tells the truth about itself - which service it's actually reading from, and when it had to switch. The same pattern applies to any external dependency. The next candidate is XMTP message fetching.

## FARCASTER / X THREAD DRAFT

**Post 1:**
Week 43 at ZAO. The big thing we shipped: a failover seam across every read-only API path in ZAOOS. Farcaster, music, members, social - all route through Hypersnap with a logged switch. Infrastructure that knows when it's failing.

**Post 2:**
ZAO Cards Phase B is up. Browser-based card editor at /cards/create. React-konva, runs fully in the browser. Phase A logic is in. Next: wire it into the nav so members can actually use it.

**Post 3:**
Six rules tightened this week from the mistakes review. The one I keep thinking about: "merged ≠ live until the running copy matches origin/main." Four bugs stayed in production for days because everyone assumed the merge meant the fix was running. It wasn't.

**Post 4:**
Measured ZAO's actual per-turn AI cost for real: ~$0.15/turn on average. By model: Fable 5.1 $0.27, Opus 5.5 $0.15, Sonnet 5.5 $0.03, Haiku 5.5 $0.01. The "Opus plans, Haiku scans, Sonnet ships" pattern from this week is the cost discipline in practice.

**Post 5:**
Still aging: Next.js CVE (110 days, one npm command), deal memos to 4 verbal confirms (37 days, written, just need to send). The gap between "done" and "shipped" is still the hardest part.
